thread:
maria: FYI AcmeRetail opened a ticket — seeing ~8-12% 429s for the last 35m, across us-east-1 and us-west-2. They claim no config changes on their side. Can someone own triage?

leo: I'll pull edge metrics. Do we have their RPM/TPM time-series? link: https://console.redwood/metrics/acmeretail/limits

ingrid: pulling logs now. On our side, their account shows bursts hitting the 500 RPM / 6000 TPM threshold. But the pattern looks very periodic — big microbursts every 120s.

dave: periodic microbursts usually mean a scheduled job with fanout. Any evidence of client retries clustering?

acmeretail: (acmeretail) We run a small worker pool (8 instances) kicking off a sync every 2 minutes. No new deployments. We do retry 1s on 429s, capped, no jitter.

leo: that explains it. token-bucket refill aligns with their schedule: the bucket refills in lumps so when the sync finishes, many workers send at once -> transient overshoot -> 429s -> synchronized retries -> retry storm.

maria: can we confirm if 429 responses include Retry-After and what value?

ingrid: logs show Retry-After: 2 frequently. sample lines: 
```
[2026-03-17T19:20:00Z] req=rx100 cust=acmeretail status=429 retry_after=2 cur_rpm=502
[2026-03-17T19:20:01Z] req=rx101 cust=acmeretail status=429 retry_after=2
[2026-03-17T19:20:02Z] req=rx102 cust=acmeretail status=200
```

dave: so clients wait fixed 1-2s and then hammer again. Jitter missing -> oscillation.

maria: immediate ask to customer: add jitter and reduce concurrency per-job. How fast can you push a change?

acmeretail: we can ship a tiny change to add random jitter (0-800ms) and reduce workers to 5 within 30m.

leo: good. Meanwhile ops options: 1) temporary soft-burst (+30% RPM for 1h) via ops UI; 2) enable smoothing (spread refill evenly) for their account; 3) enable short-lived request queuing at the edge (adds up to 250ms delay, trades latency for smoothing). Smoothing is lowest friction.

maria: if smoothing, what's the cli?

ingrid: admin CLI (internal) — slightly different command for audit: 
```
# smooth refill across window (seconds)
rwctl accounts set --acct acmeretail --smoothing=enabled --smoothing-window=60 --note="customer-sync-2m-burst"
```

ops-bot: @maria change-request-112233 logged. requires ops-oncall signoff for soft-burst or smoothing toggle for production accounts.

maria: paging ops-oncall — can we approve smoothing toggle for 60m while they deploy client change?

ops-oncall (dave): approving smoothing for 60m now. will not increase quota. If they still have 429s after client change and smoothing, we can authorize a 1h soft-burst uplift.

leo: enabling smoothing... done. We'll monitor the next 2 windows.

ingrid: metrics: after smoothing turned on, per-second refill variance drops and 429s fell from ~10% -> ~2.2% in the first 10 minutes. Looks promising.

maria: customer notified — they will also roll jitter + concurrency cap in 30m. We'll keep smoothing active until we confirm stable rates.

dave: runbook summary I'll paste into the ticket: 1) verify account RPM/TPM vs observed usage; 2) verify scheduler alignment and fanout; 3) check client retry behavior (fixed vs jittered); 4) recommend client changes (jitter + lower concurrency + progressive backoff); 5) short-term server-side options (smoothing toggle, temporary soft-burst, request queuing); 6) monitor 2 refill windows after change.

maria: adding a snippet we can share with customers for best-practices: 
```
// client-side retry pseudo
backoff = min(2, base * 2^attempt) // cap at 2s
jitter = random(0, base_jitter_ms)
sleep(backoff + jitter)
// and limit concurrent workers per sync to <=5
```

csm-zoe: copying runbook + summary to the customer ticket with steps and expected timeline. thanks team. :thumbsup:

maria: follow-up: if smoothing alone had not helped we would: 1) temporary soft-burst uplift, 2) ask customer for staggered start windows, or 3) escalate to infra for longer-term token-bucket tuning. For now smoothing + client jitter sufficed. Closing loop in 45m after full deploy.

acmeretail: thanks for the quick assist — we'll roll the change and report back.

leo: note to eng-docs: add a short doc on "scheduler alignment" and add an example to the dashboard UX to show per-second refill variance so customers can spot this pattern.
